spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


**
¶2:** All these aff
ections that are
 perceived
 in
 the
 mind
, and every
 other
 living
 state
 that
 st
irs within the natural
 man
, are
 confirmed in three modes
 of origin
. Some arise
 from incomplete
 and
 malformed begin
nings —
 interior
 states
 that never
 reached
 their
 proper
 spiritual
 form. Others, however, take
 shape
 from what
 is inherent in their own quality
,
 config
uring themselves according to the
 ruling
 love
 from
 which they spring
.

**¶3:** The
 sust
enance of these
 aff
ections is likewise
 threefold.
 There
 is wisdom
 within
 them
, if they are
 willing
 to receive it. Some
 feed
 upon
 interior
 tru
ths and the
 goods
 of life produced
 from
 them —
 they
 draw
 nourishment from interior
 tru
ths and from works
.
 And
 all
 of
 them
, in their
 entire
ty, express
 three
 fundamental spiritual
 patterns
 according
 to their origin
 and according
 to the duration
 of their life
 in
 the natural
 mind. There
 they
 are held
 fast
,
 each
 within
 its own governing
 love
.
 The Divine
 Mediator extends
 influence
 into
 all the
 capac
ities of the mind.

**
¶4:** Consider
 now the most
 elementary forms
 of natural knowledge — name
 them collectively
: first
 grow
ths and rud
iment
ary cogn
itions. From
 these were
 also
 formed per
ceptions ro
oted in evil
,
 per
ceptions bitter
 with
 falsity, per
ceptions without any
 firmness of truth
, and fals
ities that wound and obstruct —
 and
 every
 similar
 state
 that belongs
 to their
 kind
.

**¶5:** For
 that
 intention
 belongs to the self
-loves
 that
 dev
our living affections.
 Yet
 those
 states
 that were
 planted as
 rud
imentary cognitions and
 simple
 natural goods remain
 such
 in
 their essence. Nevertheless, the
 intention
 that desc
ends from the ruling
 self
-loves —
 ins
ofar as it is received
 first
 into
 works
 and natural knowledge and
 is
 *
not
* impl
anted into
 the
 self
hood of
 prop
rial will and
 understanding — forms
 per
ceptions that yield
 genuine goods sust
aining spiritual life;
 and the
 natural
 goods they
 produce are truly
 del
ightful.

**¶6
:** But
 again:
 the
 intention
 that descends from governing
 loves which
 *
both
* consume
 living
 affections *
and* appropriate natural knowledge and
 simple
 natural good
 — this forms
 perceptions that can
 produce
 nothing
 that
 sust
ains the
 spirit
. The
 works
 arising
 from them belong
 neither
 to genuine
 good nor to confirmed
 evil;
 they are spiritually inert,
 yiel
ding nothing to
 either
 side
.

“Also, their nourishment is thre[e ...] light in them, if they shall wish [...]. [...] they eat see[ds and] fr[uit ...]; they eat seeds and fruit. The [...] it entirely, and they [...] the three archetyp[es] from their nature and the [...] the time when they are on the ea[rth ...]; they are seized [...] in their [...]. The Ambassador [...] all powers [...].
“[N] it [...], first [...]. Plant them generally to this name: shoots and grass. It formed the bad, bitter trees, the reeds and the thorns and the [...] and these others that are like them.

“For that thought belongs to the flesh-eating rulers. Still, these [that were] planted (belong to) grass and gourds, since they are in their essence. Nevertheless, [this t]ho[ugh]t that came down from the rulers, as they are in fruit and grass first and shall not be planted in flesh and blood, it formed the trees that shall give nourishing fru[it], as their gourds are sweet.

“Again, this thou[ght] that came down from the powers that eat m[ea]t and also eat grass and gourds, it has formed the trees that shall not produce any nourishment. Their fruits belong neither to good nor evil.”
